This run found EMPIRICALLY that the ~1.0-1.5K ceiling §1a describes for an arbitrary return value in fact also binds a bare `text.slice(i,i+N)` return once N exceeds ~1,000-1,100 chars (tested N=8000, 1200: both truncated with a [TRUNCATED] marker; N=1000, 800: both returned complete). Used N=900 for every slice this run as the empirically-verified safe unit — smaller than §1a's stated ceiling, per its own 'a smaller slice is always safe' instruction. Logged as a new defect against §1a's text (defects_found[0]).
slice_extraction_law_applied.verification_per_slice: Each slice's returned length was checked against the requested window and its head/tail ~40 chars logged before acceptance; two slices in 32019R1242 came back [BLOCKED: Cookie/query string data] and were recovered by halving to 450-char sub-slices per §1a's fallback (recorded honestly, not silently patched over).
slice_extraction_law_applied.rebuild_by_script: Every source-<celex>.txt was rebuilt from empty by Node.js script only — either direct programmatic writes from in-session extraction results, or (for the four largest documents) by processing the harness's own persisted browser_batch tool-result JSON files with a Node script (stripping tool-call markers, dropping the trailing 'Tab Context' metadata block, concatenating slices in order) — never by manual retyping.
slice_extraction_law_applied.integrity_check_used: SHA-256 (crypto.subtle.digest in-page vs. Node crypto.createHash locally) rather than the head/tail-80-char spot check MINT-RUNBOOK.md suggests — a strictly stronger, definitive full-string-equality proof, computed for every one of the six documents and matching on every one.

metrics.fetched_length_delta_note: All six current live-fetch lengths are 0.3%-1.3% SHORTER than mint-run-001.json's originally recorded fetched-length figures, consistently across all six documents. Root cause investigated and attributed to extraction-method normalization, not page content change: this run's measurement uses the DOM node's .textContent with whitespace collapsed to single spaces (`.replace(/\s+/g,' ').trim()`), matching the format already used elsewhere in these payloads' result_content fields, whereas the figures recorded in mint-run-001.json/BATCH-001-REPORT-v2.md's fetch table were taken from an in-page raw-length read (e.g. innerText/full textContent) that preserves multiple/trailing whitespace runs as multiple characters. A uniform small shrink across all six independently-fetched documents, rather than isolated to one, is consistent with a measurement-convention difference rather than six coincidental live edits to EUR-Lex act text. Recorded honestly rather than silently reconciled; not treated as evidence of page drift.

defects_found.description: MINT-RUNBOOK.md §1a's stated <=8,000-char javascript_tool slice ceiling ('round-trips complete and untruncated in practice') does not hold: this run empirically found the return-value channel truncates a bare `text.slice(i,i+N)` return once N exceeds roughly 1,000-1,100 characters, not 8,000 — tested directly (N=8000 and N=1200 both truncated with a [TRUNCATED] marker; N=1000 and N=800 both returned complete). All extraction this run used N=900 slices instead, per §1a's own fallback instruction ('a smaller slice is always safe... NEVER quietly accept a truncated slice as close enough').
defects_found.root_cause: Unconfirmed from this session alone — plausibly a client- or tool-side response-size cap on the javascript_tool return channel that does not scale with the literal string-slice bound requested, independent of the requested slice length. Not investigated further here since the ≤900-char workaround is reliable and $0.

defects_found.description: This run's local git checkout of `master` (801cbadd) was one commit behind origin/master (9282aa3c) and still carried the PRE-hardening validate-mint-payload.mjs (250 lines: no capture-completeness gate, no unicode-integrity gate) and payload-schema.json, despite `git fetch` having been run. All six payloads were validated against this stale, weaker validator on the first pass without the discrepancy being noticed. Caught mid-run by diffing local `master` against `origin/master` for fsi-app/scripts/mint/*, which showed a 342-line/19-line diff on exactly the two files the task named as 'the hardened validator now on master.' Every validator run reported as authoritative in this artifact's per_item[] was then re-executed against the genuine origin/master validate-mint-payload.mjs + payload-schema.json (fetched verbatim via `git show origin/master:<path>` into a scratch directory, so the local worktree/checkout — shared with many other active git worktrees under /root/work/wt-* — was never touched or checked out). All six payloads pass identically under the real hardened validator (confirmed by re-running, not assumed).
defects_found.root_cause: `git fetch` updates remote-tracking refs (origin/master) but does not move the local `master` branch pointer or its checked-out working tree; this repo's local `master` had its own commit (801cbadd, 'Memory: Addendum 73') layered on an older base and was never fast-forwarded or merged to origin/master's 9282aa3c inside this session, so `origin/master` and the local `master` used by default in fsi-app/ diverged silently.
defects_found.fix_ref: Not a code fix — a process fix applied within this run: validator invocations for this artifact's per_item[] verdicts were run against files fetched directly from origin/master via `git show`, bypassing the stale local checkout entirely, rather than modifying the shared local git state (git checkout/merge/rebase of `master` was deliberately avoided to not disturb other concurrent worktrees on this branch).

defects_found.description: payload-32015R0757.json's jurisdictional_scope claim's source_span/claim_text ('...as well as within ports under the jurisdiction of a Member State.') was missing the words 'of call' present in the true source ('...as well as within ports of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State.'). Caught by the hardened validator's fact_span_not_in_source check once result_content held the real, byte-verified full text; the old excerpt-shaped capture had apparently been hand-transcribed close enough to itself to self-validate.
defects_found.root_cause: Batch-001's original hand-transcription (pre-hardening) copied the claim span from an incomplete/earlier reading of the page rather than the verbatim source, and nothing at the time cross-checked it against an independently archived full capture.
defects_found.fix_ref: payload-32015R0757.json: source_span, claim_text, full_brief, and the relevant sections[].content_md corrected to the verbatim source substring located via indexOf() against source-32015R0757.txt (4 occurrences fixed programmatically) — this run.

defects_found.description: payload-32023R0956.json's jurisdictional_scope claim had TWO discrepancies against the true source: (1) it used straight quotes 'CBAM' where the live source uses curly quotes ‘CBAM’ (U+2018/U+2019, confirmed by codepoint inspection); (2) it said 'the goods' where the true source says 'the goods listed in Annex I'. This directly contradicts BATCH-001-REPORT-v2.md's prior claim of having already fixed the curly-vs-straight-quote bug for this document — that earlier 'fix' was itself wrong relative to the genuine live EUR-Lex source once independently re-verified this run.
defects_found.root_cause: Same class as 32015R0757 above: a prior session's manual quote-direction correction was made without a freshly re-verified, byte-exact full-text reference to check it against, so it could not actually be confirmed correct at the time it was made.
defects_found.fix_ref: payload-32023R0956.json: source_span corrected to the exact verbatim true-source substring (verified present in source-32023R0956.txt via indexOf() before writing); all straight-quote 'CBAM' occurrences in full_brief/sections/claim_text updated to curly ‘CBAM’, and 'embedded in goods listed in Annex I' corrected to 'embedded in the goods listed in Annex I' throughout, for consistency beyond the strict validator requirement — this run.
